links.outcome: Adenoma detection rate by session time with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Unassisted ADR early vs late sessions 13.73% vs 5.70% (P=.005); with AI 22.95% vs 22.06% (P=.78). AI assistance OR 3.81 in late vs 1.60 in early sessions.
links.quote: After the intervention of the AI system, as expected, no statistically significant difference was found (22.95% vs 22.06%, P = .78; OR, 0.96; 95% CI; 0.71-1.29).

links.outcome: ADR improvement with AI-assisted versus unassisted colonoscopy in randomized trials
links.effect: AI-assisted colonoscopy raised ADR and eliminated early-late session gap; AI OR 3.81 (2.10-6.91) in late sessions and 1.60 (1.10-2.34) in early sessions.
links.quote: Furthermore, the AI systems showed better assistance ability on ADR in late sessions compared with early sessions (odds ratio, 3.81; 95% CI, 2.10-6.91 vs 1.60; 95% CI, 1.10-2.34).

unlisted_practices: Using AI assistance to offset time-of-day (fatigue-related) decline in clinician performance

screen.reason: This study is a secondary analysis of two prospective randomized controlled trials evaluating the clinical effect of an AI computer-aided detection system during real colonoscopies across different times of day to see if it mitigates fatigue-related quality drops. It tests the core clinical utility of AI assistance rather than a specific deployment guardrail or organizational implementation practice.
